svg.title: Figure 2. Ports, native and introduced floras, sea geometry and mapped host-isolation gradients
svg.desc: The first two panels show source-adjusted port coefficients and native versus alien Jaccard overlap of 126 island floras. Panel C shows a distinct 104-island electrical resistance prediction for native and introduced plant similarities in source and strict both-islands-unseen tests; these are not historical current observations.
svg.text: 2 | Ports and two layers of island floras
Contemporary WCVP accepted plants; matched botanical island regions
Area and TDWG Level1 adjusted; n = 126 regions
Does marine electrical resistance help predict plant similarity?
104 botanical islands | 5,355 source Jaccard pairs | undirected uniform-ocean circuit
MSE reduction; whiskers are descriptive source intervals (not independent geographic replications)
Matched port-flora: 126 islands. Marine-circuit prediction: separate 104-island source cohort.
Strict five-fold interval includes zero; circuit resistance is not measured directional ocean flow or vessel cargo.
Mainland isolation and candidate butterfly food
Original fixed 239-host panel, 126 botanical islands; area, latitude, ports and Level1 adjusted
Model-fitted known-host opportunities, not butterfly presence. Distance uses approximate WGSRPD3 island-to-mainland boundaries.
Nine-Level1 slope-shift test: p = 0.068; cannot infer ship transport or demographic compensation.
